modules.behavior: Iterative AES-128 encryption sequencer (FIPS-197) with a valid/ready-style input and output; the handshake ports are plain protocol none signals. Blocks are 128-bit big-endian byte strings: byte 0 is bits [127:120]. Registers, all reset to 0: busy, out_valid, rnd[3:0], ct[127:0] (the state), rk[127:0] (the round key). Outputs, all views of registered state: in_ready = !busy && !out_valid; out_valid; ct; rk; last = (rnd == 10); rcon = 01, 02, 04, 08, 10, 20, 40, 80, 1b, 36 (hex) for rnd = 0..9 and 00 for rnd = 10..15. Neighbours: round_out = AES round of (ct, round key rk, final round = last); key_next = key-schedule step of (rk, rcon). At each rising edge with rst low, using pre-edge values: if busy: rk = key_next; then if rnd == 0 (key preparation) rnd = 1; else ct = round_out and, when rnd == 10, busy = 0, out_valid = 1, rnd = 0, otherwise rnd = rnd + 1. Else if out_valid: out_valid = 0 when out_ready = 1 (ct holds). Else (idle) if in_valid = 1: accept: ct = pt ^ key (initial AddRoundKey), rk = key, rnd = 0, busy = 1. key, pt and in_valid are ignored except at the accepting edge, out_ready only while out_valid. An accepted block takes 11 busy edges (key preparation, rounds 1..10) and out_valid with ct = ciphertext appears after the 11th; the next block can be accepted at the edge after the output transfer at the earliest. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns every register to its reset value; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the registers in state and return every output as it is after that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled.
modules.name: aes_ctrl

modules.behavior: Combinational AES encryption round (FIPS-197). Bytes are big-endian: byte n (0..15) of a 128-bit value is bits [127-8n:120-8n], and byte n sits at row n % 4, column n // 4 of the state. state_out = AddRoundKey(MixColumns(ShiftRows(SubBytes(state_in))), round_key) when final_round = 0, and AddRoundKey(ShiftRows(SubBytes(state_in)), round_key) when final_round = 1. SubBytes applies the AES S-box to every byte (the multiplicative inverse in GF(2^8) modulo x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1, 0 mapping to 0, followed by the affine map b ^ rotl(b,1) ^ rotl(b,2) ^ rotl(b,3) ^ rotl(b,4) ^ 0x63; S(00) = 63, S(01) = 7c, S(53) = ed). ShiftRows rotates row r left by r: new byte at (r, c) = old byte at (r, (c + r) % 4). MixColumns maps each column (a0, a1, a2, a3), a0 at row 0, to (2a0^3a1^a2^a3, a0^2a1^3a2^a3, a0^a1^2a2^3a3, 3a0^a1^a2^2a3) in GF(2^8). AddRoundKey is a 128-bit XOR. Python oracle: combinational and stateless; step returns the outputs for this step's inputs (latency 0, no clock and no reset port).
modules.name: aes_round

modules.behavior: Combinational AES-128 key-schedule step (FIPS-197 KeyExpansion, one round key at a time). key_in = {w0, w1, w2, w3} with w0 = key_in[127:96]; temp = SubWord(RotWord(w3)) ^ {rcon, 24 zero bits}, where RotWord({a0, a1, a2, a3}) = {a1, a2, a3, a0} (a0 the most significant byte) and SubWord applies the AES S-box (as in aes_round) to each byte; w4 = w0 ^ temp, w5 = w1 ^ w4, w6 = w2 ^ w5, w7 = w3 ^ w6; key_out = {w4, w5, w6, w7}. rcon is used as given (any 8-bit value). Python oracle: combinational and stateless; step returns the outputs for this step's inputs (latency 0, no clock and no reset port).
modules.name: aes_key_step

implementation.meaning: Out-of-context implementation (chip_top_flow_for_soc_block): the top is a block inside a larger design, synthesized with synth_design -mode out_of_context and placed and routed without I/O buffers or package pins. clk is constrained at the target period and modeled as driven by a global clock buffer (HD.CLK_SRC). Data ports have no input or output delay and no pad delay, so they are unconstrained I/O; the routed WNS and WHS, and timing acceptance, cover the internal clocked paths only, and combinational logic between a port and its first or last register is not timed. Utilization excludes I/O buffers.

metric_provenance: Structured metrics are parsed from retained reports; routed utilization/timing reports take precedence when present. The manifest identifies complete files by hash. Header excerpts are bounded previews, not complete reports or an independent metric source.
objective_policy: First establish timing feasibility. A verified timing-feasible candidate may replace a known timing-infeasible previous best even with higher area or power; classify this as timing_recovery, not objective savings. While the previous best is timing-infeasible, a verified still-infeasible candidate with strictly better setup WNS and hold not worse beyond a small tolerance may replace it as timing_progress, which is not closure; a feasible candidate always outranks it. Once both are timing-feasible, require strict improvement of the chosen objective; for maximize_freq that is register-to-register setup slack (reg2reg_wns_ns) when both designs report it, otherwise full setup WNS for both, while feasibility stays on full WNS and WHS. minimize_luts compares (lut_used, ff_used) and minimize_ffs compares (ff_used, lut_used) lexicographically: an equal primary metric with a strictly lower secondary is an objective improvement, a higher primary never is, and a secondary missing from either design gives no tie-break. Unknown or contradictory incumbent timing evidence cannot establish recovery. A completed experiment may find no improvement. Do not invent mandatory savings, slack margins, tool versions, timing corners, new tests, thresholds, code-style quotas or external environment requirements.
